cells.tense: A real piece of what comes next is in your hand right now, and you can hold it a moment longer.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Give one person one useful piece of help this week, all the way to done. Finish it yourself, then step back. No follow-ups, no extra offers.
cells.core:
Something real is in your hand — a thing you could start, a piece of help you could give — and you can feel it without spending it yet. That's what you do well here: you read how much is needed, add a little, take a little, and stay level with what's already moving. You don't force it and you don't crush it. So the help you give lands and holds.

Much of the time you're in the middle of something already underway. The help that goes right is a clean piece, given to someone who needs it, carried to the end. Give one such piece this week and finish it, then step back. Stepping back lets the other person stand on their own, which is what the help was for.
cells.sheetLine: Give one real piece of help, finish it, then hands off.
cells.verb: bringing a thing into its first form, given in the hand before it is spent
cells.place: where what is added and what is taken away each keeps their flow, in the middle of what is already running

cells.tense: You're bracing for how the next thing will land before anything has been handed to you.
cells.act: know the feeling fully before you move on
cells.ask: Put every feeling that's here on a single page before you decide on anything, all of them, none crossed out. Do it once this week, then leave the page.
cells.core:
Something wants to start — a plan, a resource, a thing you could build — and you're already three moves into how it will land before the first move is handed to you. On ground like this, that looks like constant course-correcting before anything has been poured. The care underneath is real; the tight grip on top is what others meet as pressure, mostly by how tired they get.

What's thin is the feeling underneath, felt whole. Before you set the next thing going, put every feeling that's here on a single page — none crossed out — and read the whole of it without editing. It doesn't decide anything. It means what's in you is fully in you before you step, and then the step comes from something whole.

cells.tense: This place moved on, and you're still at the spot where something was set down.
cells.act: see it whole, with nothing hidden
cells.ask: Sit with one tangle long enough to see all of it with nothing left out — the whole shape at once, no part skipped. Then close the notebook for now.
cells.core:
A concrete thing could start — a resource, a hand reached out with something in it — and you're not picking it up. You're somewhere in the middle of something already running, and the ordinary give-and-take that keeps things level has gone quiet. The moment has moved past, and you're at the spot where something was set down, not lifting it.

Seeing is what pulls you back, not effort. Sit with one tangle long enough to see all of it with nothing left out — the whole shape at once, no part skipped. You're not deciding yet. Let the full shape show, and once it's all there the next step is a thing you can pick up again.

cells.tense: You keep the whole thing level, and you'd tell anyone it just runs this way.
cells.ask: Choose a place you quietly keep steady and sit with it until nothing about it is left unseen — the whole of it, plain. Then put it away and tell no one.
cells.core:
You're holding a lot of pieces in their right proportions — adding here, taking away there, keeping the whole thing running — and your version is that it isn't anything, it's just how this works. It isn't just how this works. That constant adjusting is what you do. You talk about it like background noise, and some part of you would rather it stay background.

Before all of this, there was someone who just saw a thing clearly. Choose a place you quietly keep steady and sit with it until nothing about it is left unseen — the whole of it, plain. Then put it away; nobody else has to read it. The hand doing the seeing is the same one doing the work.
